tooling.message:
feat(check): lernapps check runs the checks of the built app and reports in YAML

## Intent

Step 3 of the plan (#12): one check command for hooks, CI and the listing validation. It runs the toolchain steps of a repo and the checks of the built app, also on a built folder or a URL without the repo, checks a catalog entry against its app, and gives one report that people and assistants can act on.

## Key changes

- `lernapps check --pre-commit` runs format, lint and types; `--pre-push` runs unit tests, build, the checks of the built app, a licence check of the dependencies and the Playwright tests. The CLI runs every check whose input exists and decides nothing from rule metadata.
- Each page reachable from the start page is visited once in Chromium without a click. Requests to other hosts are recorded and blocked, so no check depends on another server.
- New checks, each with its rule id: no-request-before-click, no-tracking, readable-without-javascript, usable-at-360px, accessible (axe-core), links-resolve, dependency-licence, site-check, entry-links-resolve and entry-fitness-matches. Failed toolchain steps are findings of checks-pass. Skill sections carry the ids where an assistant can prevent the problem; the catalog grows from 20 to 26 rules.
- A passing run prints one line; otherwise a YAML report with a published JSON Schema. A failed pre-push adds one to prePushFailures in the plan file.
- The Playwright fixture is served on 127.0.0.1, since localhost resolves to ::1 on the CI runner.
- The plan marks step 3 done and lists the gaps it left: no in-place suppressions, fitness only before a click, no fetching of external links, licences only in the repo, `--site` given by hand.

## Dependencies and side effects

- yaml and @lernapps/site become dependencies; playwright and axe-core are new.

tooling.message:
feat(preset): the shared preset, its lint plugin and the git hooks every app extends

## Intent

Step 4 of the plan (#13): what every app imports and never edits. An app that only extends the preset gets every lint rule and both git hooks without configuration of its own, so a rule or hook changed in the package reaches every app with the next version.

## Key changes

- `lernapps()` from @lernapps/tooling/preset is the whole vite-plus configuration: lint with the plugin and each rule's severity, no `any`, type-aware checks, format, unit tests, staged files. An app needs one line in vite.config.ts, a tsconfig.json that extends the package's, and a prepare script.
- The package brings a Playwright setup (desktop and 360 px), a storage wrapper under the app's prefix, a translator for message files and helpers for assistive technology.
- The hooks are scripts in the package, installed by the vite-plus dispatcher: pre-commit runs `lernapps check --pre-commit`, pre-push `lernapps check --pre-push`.
- An Oxlint plugin with one file per rule; every message links to its rule. New rules: storage-through-wrapper, suppression-reason, keep-the-preset and strict-typescript; no-request-before-click and learner-text-german also get lint rules. `any` uses Oxlint's own rule.
- A fixture app installed from git proves it end to end: a lint error stops the commit, a request to another host stops the push and counts a failure, a clean commit and push pass.
- The architecture names how the hooks and lint rules are built.

## Dependencies and side effects

- New package exports (preset, tsconfig, playwright, storage, i18n, a11y, lint); vite-plus becomes a peer dependency.

tooling.message:
feat(review): review procedure with prompt, rubric per archetype and verdict schema

## Intent

Step 8 of the plan (#17), the judgment part of the listing validation: an agent in a fresh context reviews an app that asks to be listed, starting from the check report, and writes a verdict bound to the reviewed commit. Every finding names a rule id or proposes a new rule.

## Key changes

- review/prompt.md is the prompt for a fresh agent: clone the app at the commit, build it, run lernapps check, read the report, rules, plan, rubric, bundle and history, judge, write and check verdict.yaml.
- The rubric has one file for all apps and one per archetype; every item needs its rubric block.
- New rules with rubric item and skill section: no-learner-data-in-texts, correct-content-support (hint) and one per archetype: topic-has-exercises, start-page-explains, quiz-feedback-explains.
- The verdict is YAML with a published JSON Schema; it fails exactly when a finding is an error. `npm run verdict` checks a verdict against the schema and the rule catalog.
- CI calls no model: a verdict recorded by a fresh agent for a fixture app with a planted ad must fail it on no-ads.
- The architecture gets the review block, the verdict interface, the listing scenario, a decision and a glossary term.

tooling.message:
feat(quiz): lernapps create and the quiz archetype

## Intent

Step 6 of the plan (#15), the first archetype as a deep scaffold: `lernapps create --archetype quiz` plus a question bank gives an app that passes `lernapps check` without further code. The creator's assistant writes only questions and options.

## Key changes

- `lernapps create` copies the archetype's folder from lernapps/app-templates at a commit pinned in package.json, or from a local clone for the tests. It writes AGENTS.md, the plan, a Pages workflow that runs the check, an issue form for content errors, LICENSE and renovate.json. It refuses an unknown archetype and a folder that is not empty.
- The quiz engine lives in the package: a build step validates src/quiz.json and renders every question into the page, so it reads as a worksheet with an answer key without JavaScript. In the browser it shows one question at a time in a seeded order, with deep links, feedback, score and solutions.
- The question bank has a published JSON Schema plus checks the schema cannot express; every problem names the question.
- Generic Playwright tests for any bank give every quiz app tests of its own content.
- The skill lernapps-quiz has eight rules for the archetype.
- The pin points at the head of the app-templates branch with the quiz template, until that pull request is merged.

## Dependencies and side effects

- Needs the quiz template in app-templates (78cea92, app-templates#2).
- CI checks out app-templates at the pinned commit for the generator's tests.

tooling.message:
test: remove temporary test folders; mark plan steps 4 and 8 done

## Intent

Every end-to-end run left fresh clones with node_modules in /tmp. With several agents testing at once, they filled the disk and blocked pushes. The plan must also show steps 4 and 8 as merged.

## Key changes

- Temporary folders live under one root per test file, created on first use and removed after its tests. A full check now leaves no folder behind.
- The plan marks the shared preset (step 4) and the review procedure (step 8) as done.

app-templates.message:
feat(quiz): the template of the quiz archetype

## Intent

Step 6 of the plan needs a folder for `lernapps create --archetype quiz` to copy: a working quiz that passes `lernapps check`, in which the app supplies only its question bank.

## Key changes

- Only thin files: vite.config.ts uses the quiz preset of @lernapps/tooling, main.ts starts the engine, the end-to-end test runs the package's generic tests on the app's bank, and index.html holds the marker where the build renders the questions.
- An example bank in German with one question of each of the six types, so the creator's assistant sees every type.
- @lernapps/tooling is pinned to a commit with a lockfile, so `npm ci` works in the folder and in a generated app.
- A workflow checks every template folder with `lernapps check`; the README describes the repo as the templates of the archetypes.

## Dependencies and side effects

- The generator and engine are in tooling (daf6569, db0d98e on the branch of tooling#36).
